title: llm-routing-fallback-scratchpad - user stories + rough PRD
body:
Context:
- Quick scratchpad for routing + fallback behavior across model variants and capacity tiers.
content:
Problem statement:
- Customers run critical LLM features (search, summarization, chat) and need predictable latency and cost.
- When preferred model (e.g., high-accuracy/slow) is overloaded or unavailable, we should failover gracefully to compatible variants without hurting quality too much or violating SLOs.
- Need flexible policy primitives (latency/cost/accuracy) + observability and rollout controls.

Goals / success metrics (rough):
- 99.5% of requests served within customer SLOs using configured routing policies (can be multi-tier: primary, fallback, degraded).
- Degradation path keeps functional correctness (e.g., preserve hallucination thresholds for NER/QA) — measure via A/B evals on key prompt sets.
- Reduce outage-induced errors by 80% vs no-fallback baseline.
- Provide clear per-request reason for fallback in traces for debugging.

Primary personas:
- Product engineers embedding LLM features (care about latency and cost).
- Platform engineers (set org-level routing defaults and safety policies).
- SRE / on-call (need predictable behavior and observability).

User stories (rough backlog order):
1) As a product engineer, I want to specify a routing policy for a route that prefers model-A but will fallback to model-B if latency > 300ms or capacity 100% so my users don't see timeouts.
2) As a platform admin, I want org-level default fallbacks that can be overridden per-route so teams get sane defaults.
3) As an SRE, I want traces to show "fallback-reason" and target model id so I can triage spikes quickly.
4) As a product engineer, I want configurable quality filters (e.g., minimum average eval score on a prompt-set) to avoid falling back to models that degrade critical tasks.
5) As a developer, I want a simulation mode that runs routing logic on historical traffic to estimate cost & latency impact before enabling.
6) As a customer using Dedicated, I want fallback to prefer Dedicated capacity first, then Hosted, then sparse Private variants (policy order depends on customer preference).

Behavioral primitives (ideas):
- Policy predicates: latency threshold, queue length, scheduled maintenance flag, error rate, token-cost budget, model-eval delta.
- Fallback chain: ordered list of compatible models + quantization variants (e.g., quantized-8 -> int8 -> fp16) with compatibility rules (tokenizer, API contract).
- Soft vs hard fallback: soft = routed to fallback only after X errors; hard = immediate when predicate met.
- Graceful degrade: try partial responses or lower max_tokens if model cost budget hit.
- Canary/rollout: percent-based routing to new model variant with automatic revert if eval regressions exceed threshold.

Observability + UX:
- Per-request metadata: routed_model, fallback_reason, route_policy_id, estimated_cost_delta.
- Console view: heatmap of fallback events by route/model; time-series of fallback rate and reasons; quick links to last N traces.
- Alerts: routing oscillation detection + high fallback rate per route.

Open questions / risks:
- How to define "compatible" model variants automatically? Need tokenizer / output-contract checks.
- For multi-turn chat with KV cache, switching model mid-conversation can break cache. Options: disable fallback mid-conversation, or warm KV cache on fallback warm-up.
- Billing implications: if fallback goes to cheaper model, do we bill original route? Need clear docs and invoicing behavior.
- Privacy/tenancy: Dedicated customers may not want Hosted fallback — design policy precedence and opt-out.

Prototype plan (MVP):
- Phase 1 (4w): simple routing predicate (latency threshold + capacity) + ordered fallback list per route. Expose as route config (JSON). Basic tracing and console list.
- Phase 2 (6w): add quality predicate (link to eval scores on prompt-sets), simulation mode, per-org defaults, and simple canary rollout.
- Phase 3 (PR): multi-turn cache handling, cost-aware fallback, billing contract updates, more advanced predicates (error-rate, token-cost).

Edge cases / implementation notes:
- Model semantics: ensure API contract compatibility (function-calling, tool interfaces). If incompatible, skip variant.
- Rate-limiting: when fallback happens we still need to respect quotas across capacity pools to avoid cascading failures.
- Backpressure: consider circuit-breaker that temporarily disables a target model for N minutes if error-rate spike detected.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Sync with SRE + serving-runtime to understand how to detect "capacity" in real-time (metrics, headroom). @Zoe to get SRE metric list.
- Draft sample route config schema (JSON) for review.
- Small prototype: router that evaluates policies against synthetic latency/capacity events.
- Link up with billing to confirm accounting for fallback hops.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Might be good to have "degraded-response" mode: lower-k max_tokens + structured output only to save cost and maintain correctness for some tasks.
- Consider ML-based router that predicts which model will complete under SLO with lowest cost; later iteration.

References / related docs:
- existing routing prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-proto (PR 56).
- Confluence draft: /company/rl-routing-design.

----
Rough config sketch (informal):
{
  "route": "/summarize",
  "policy": {
    "preferred": ["redwood-m4-large"],
    "fallbacks": [{"model":"redwood-m3","predicates": [{"type":"latency","max_ms":300}]}, {"model":"open-qg","predicates":[] }],
    "quality_min_score": 0.75,
    "canary": {"pct":5, "eval_prompt_set": "summ-01"}
  }
}

(keep this in scratchpad — will formalize schema later)
